segments: Basil and Mor Ephrem justify
that the first language was the Syriac language before the division of tongues,
as even the word for 'confusion' (bulbala) bears witness.
Holy Jacob, however, and John of Yathrib are of the opinion
that Hebrew was the first language, which was preserved with Eber,
because he was righteous and did not consent to the building of the tower.
And according to others,
from Abraham,
he who crossed the rivers,
and crossed between the divisions,
and passed from the paganism of his father to faith in God,
he was called 'Hebrew'.
After Reu, Serug his son, at the age of one hundred and thirty years, begot Nahor.
And all the days of his life were three hundred and thirty years.
Now in his days, minted coinage and jewelry from Ophir appeared.
And men made idols to demons,
and they were aided by devils.
And after Nimrod,
there arose as the second king in Babel, Cambyrus (Cambros), eighty-five years, in the days of Serug.
And he fought with the people called Celts (Galatians),
and prevailed,
and confined them within the mountains that are between them.
And after Cambyrus,
there arose as the third king of the Chaldeans, Scamyros (Samirus), seventy-two years.
And he fought with the Greeks and the Canaanites, and prevailed;
and he built cities for the Parthians and for the Chaldeans.
And he was the first of them to begin making measures and scales.
And in his days silk and dyed garments appeared.
And it is related as a fable that he had three eyes and horns.
And in that same time, there arose as the second ruler in Egypt, Epiphanius, forty-six years.
And he was the first to construct a ship and ride upon the sea.
And after him arose the third ruler in Egypt, Athanophius (Aethiops?):
he who, because he fought with the Cushites and conquered them, was called by this name which translates as 'Ethiopian'.
And he killed Sheba.
And after Sheba, his daughter reigned forty years.
And from here women began to reign over the Cushites.
And after Epiphanius (Athanophius?):
there arose as the fourth king in Egypt, Pharaoh son of Sanus, thirty-five years.
And from here began the name 'Pharaoh'.
After Serug {OCR: ܤܪܬܓ݂ for ܤܪܘܿܓ݂}, Nahor his son, at the age of seventy-nine years, begot Terah.
And all the days of his life were two hundred and one years.
In this same time, Assaronos (Bassaronos) the Parthian fought with Samirus and killed him.
